# `silk/encoding/base64`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

Encode and decode standard Base64 (RFC 4648, with padding) into byte slices that you supply.

## When to use
Use [`Base64`](#Base64) when a protocol needs the standard alphabet (`A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `+`, `/`) with
`=` padding, for example HTTP Basic authentication or a JSON field. Call
[`Base64.encodedLength`](#Base64.impl.encodedLength) or [`Base64.decodedLength`](#Base64.impl.decodedLength) to get the exact size of the output, and
then [`Base64.encodeInto`](#Base64.impl.encodeInto) or [`Base64.decodeInto`](#Base64.impl.decodeInto) to write it.

## Details
The functions do not allocate. They return a `Result`, and they check all input and the size of
the output before they write the first byte. A failure does not change the output. A success
changes only the prefix that it reports.

Decoding is strict. It rejects whitespace, the URL-safe characters `-` and `_`, missing or
misplaced padding, and unused bits that are not zero, so each byte sequence has exactly one
encoding.

## Errors
The functions return a [`Base64Error`](#Base64Error). Its `reason` tells you what failed, and `offset` gives
the position in the input for a decoding error.

## Gotchas
This module has no MIME, PEM, URL-safe, unpadded, or streaming variant. Base64 is an encoding,
not encryption.

## Examples
### Encode and decode a short message
```silk
import silk.encoding.base64 { Base64, Base64Error }
import silk.core.result { Result }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut encoded: [u8; 8] = [0; 8]
  let written = match Base64.encodeInto(&mut encoded, b"Hi!?") {
    Result<usize, Base64Error>.Success { value } => value
    Result<usize, Base64Error>.Failure { error: _ } => {
      return 1
    }
  }
  // "Hi!?" encodes to "SGkhPw==".
  if written != 8 || encoded[0] != 83 || encoded[6] != 61 {
    return 1
  }
  let mut decoded: [u8; 4] = [0; 4]
  return match Base64.decodeInto(&mut decoded, &encoded) {
    Result<usize, Base64Error>.Success { value } => {
      if value != 4 || decoded[0] != 72 || decoded[3] != 63 {
        return 1
      }
      return 0
    }
    Result<usize, Base64Error>.Failure { error: _ } => 1
  }
}
```

### Reject input that is not strict Base64
```silk
import silk.encoding.base64 { Base64, Base64Error, Base64Reason }
import silk.core.option { Option }
import silk.core.result { Result }

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  // `-` is URL-safe Base64, not standard Base64.
  return match Base64.decodedLength(b"ab-d") {
    Result<usize, Base64Error>.Failure { error } => {
      if error.reason != Base64Reason.InvalidByte
        || Option<usize>.unwrapOr(move error.offset, 0) != 2 {
        return 1
      }
      return 0
    }
    Result<usize, Base64Error>.Success { value: _ } => 1
  }
}
```

## `Base64Reason`

```silk
pub enum Base64Reason
```

The cause of a [`Base64Error`](#Base64Error).

<a id="Base64Reason.InvalidLength"></a>

### `InvalidLength`

```silk
InvalidLength
```

The encoded input is not empty and its length is not a multiple of 4. `offset` is the input
length.

<a id="Base64Reason.InvalidByte"></a>

### `InvalidByte`

```silk
InvalidByte
```

An input byte is not in the standard alphabet. `offset` is its position.

<a id="Base64Reason.InvalidPadding"></a>

### `InvalidPadding`

```silk
InvalidPadding
```

`=` occurs before the last two positions, or `=` is followed by a byte that is not `=`.
`offset` is the position of the misplaced `=`, or the input length.

<a id="Base64Reason.NonCanonicalPadBits"></a>

### `NonCanonicalPadBits`

```silk
NonCanonicalPadBits
```

The last character before the padding has unused bits that are not zero, such as `QR==` in
place of `QQ==`. `offset` is its position.

<a id="Base64Reason.SizeOverflow"></a>

### `SizeOverflow`

```silk
SizeOverflow
```

The encoded length does not fit in `usize`.

<a id="Base64Reason.OutputTooSmall"></a>

### `OutputTooSmall`

```silk
OutputTooSmall
```

The output slice is too short. `required` and `available` give the two lengths.

## `Base64Error`

```silk
pub struct Base64Error
```

A Base64 failure.

Decoding errors set `offset`. `OutputTooSmall` sets `required` and `available`. The fields that
do not apply to the reason are `None`.

<a id="Base64Error.reason"></a>

### Field `reason`

```silk
pub reason: Base64Reason
```

The cause of the failure.

<a id="Base64Error.offset"></a>

### Field `offset`

```silk
pub offset: Option<usize>
```

For a decoding error, the position in the input: the bad byte for `InvalidByte` and
`NonCanonicalPadBits`, the misplaced `=` or the input length for `InvalidPadding`, and the
input length for `InvalidLength`.

<a id="Base64Error.required"></a>

### Field `required`

```silk
pub required: Option<usize>
```

For `OutputTooSmall`, the number of bytes that the output needs.

<a id="Base64Error.available"></a>

### Field `available`

```silk
pub available: Option<usize>
```

For `OutputTooSmall`, the length of the output that you gave.

## `Base64`

```silk
pub struct Base64
```

Functions for strict standard Base64 with padding (RFC 4648).

### When to use

Use it when a protocol needs the standard alphabet (`A-Z`, `a-z`, `0-9`, `+`, `/`) with `=`
padding, for example HTTP Basic authentication or a JSON field. Call [`Base64.encodedLength`](#Base64.impl.encodedLength)
or [`Base64.decodedLength`](#Base64.impl.decodedLength) to get the exact size of the output, and then
[`Base64.encodeInto`](#Base64.impl.encodeInto) or [`Base64.decodeInto`](#Base64.impl.decodeInto) to write it.

### Details

The functions do not allocate. They check all input and the size of the output before they
write the first byte. A failure does not change the output. Decoding is strict. It rejects
whitespace, the URL-safe characters `-` and `_`, missing or misplaced padding, and unused bits
that are not zero.

### Gotchas

There is no MIME, PEM, URL-safe, unpadded, or streaming variant. Base64 is an encoding, not
encryption.

<a id="Base64.impl.encodedLength"></a>

### Associated function `encodedLength`

```silk
pub fn encodedLength(inputLength: usize) -> Result<usize, Base64Error>
```

Returns the length of the Base64 text for `inputLength` bytes: 4 for each started group of 3
bytes.

Returns 0 for 0.

#### Errors
- `SizeOverflow` if the length does not fit in `usize`.

<a id="Base64.impl.decodedLength"></a>

### Associated function `decodedLength`

```silk
pub fn decodedLength(input: &[u8]) -> Result<usize, Base64Error>
```

Checks that `input` is strict Base64 and returns the number of bytes that it decodes to.

Returns 0 for empty input. Use it to size the output of [`Base64.decodeInto`](#Base64.impl.decodeInto).

Decoding is strict. It rejects whitespace, the URL-safe characters `-` and `_`, missing or
misplaced padding, and unused bits that are not zero, so each byte sequence has exactly one
encoding.

#### Errors
- `InvalidLength`, `InvalidByte`, `InvalidPadding`, or `NonCanonicalPadBits` for the first
  problem in `input`, from left to right. `offset` gives its position.

<a id="Base64.impl.encodeInto"></a>

### Associated function `encodeInto`

```silk
pub fn encodeInto(output: &mut [u8], input: &[u8]) -> Result<usize, Base64Error>
```

Writes the Base64 text of `input` to the start of `output` and returns the number of bytes
written.

It writes no NUL terminator. The bytes of `output` after the written prefix do not change.

#### Errors
- `SizeOverflow` if the encoded length does not fit in `usize`.
- `OutputTooSmall` if `output` is shorter than [`Base64.encodedLength`](#Base64.impl.encodedLength). `output` does not
  change.

<a id="Base64.impl.decodeInto"></a>

### Associated function `decodeInto`

```silk
pub fn decodeInto(output: &mut [u8], input: &[u8]) -> Result<usize, Base64Error>
```

Decodes the Base64 text `input` to the start of `output` and returns the number of bytes
written.

The bytes of `output` after the written prefix do not change.

Decoding is strict. It rejects whitespace, the URL-safe characters `-` and `_`, missing or
misplaced padding, and unused bits that are not zero, so each byte sequence has exactly one
encoding.

#### Errors
- `InvalidLength`, `InvalidByte`, `InvalidPadding`, or `NonCanonicalPadBits` if `input` is not
  strict Base64. These errors come before `OutputTooSmall`.
- `OutputTooSmall` if `output` is shorter than [`Base64.decodedLength`](#Base64.impl.decodedLength).

`output` does not change when an error occurs.
